page: Vultr vx1-g-64c-256g-3840s is a general-purpose server belonging to the VX1 Cloud Compute family. It features 64 dedicated vCPUs powered by an AMD EPYC processor with an x86_64 architecture, operating at a clock speed of 2.0 GHz. The processor configuration includes 32 physical cores with hyper-threading, supported by 48 KB L1d cache, 1.0 MB L2 cache, and 32 MB L3 cache. The system is equipped with 256.0 GB of RAM, providing 4.0 GB of memory per core, and includes 3840 GB of bundled local NVMe SSD storage.

In benchmark evaluations, this server demonstrates strong multi-core capabilities and high-tier memory throughput. The stress-ng single-core CPU performance ranks in the top 10% with a score of 3701.09, while the multi-core performance reaches 117951.61, placing it in the top 25%. Large-block memory bandwidth is highly efficient, with read-only speeds of 496.98 GB/sec and write speeds of 190.5 GB/sec, both ranking in the top 10%. However, the Passmark memory score of 2255.25 falls into the middle 50% average tier.

The hardware profile and benchmark results indicate high suitability for database operations, web serving, and moderate machine learning tasks. Passmark database operations scored in the top 10% at 35622.38, and Redis SET operations achieved 104.09 million operations per second. For language model workloads, the server processes prompts at 4461.42 tokens/sec for a small 135M model and 192.7 tokens/sec for a medium 7B model. Given the high density of dedicated AMD EPYC cores and substantial bundled NVMe storage, this server offers a resource-dense configuration for enterprise workloads requiring local storage and high parallel processing.
description: Vultr vx1-g-64c-256g-3840s is a dedicated server from the VX1 Cloud Compute family, featuring 64 vCPUs powered by an AMD EPYC processor at 2.0 GHz. It is configured with 256.0 GB of RAM and 3840 GB of local NVMe SSD storage. The server delivers top-tier performance in large-block memory bandwidth, with read speeds of 496.98 GB/sec and write speeds of 190.5 GB/sec, alongside strong multi-core processing capabilities. Benchmark results highlight its efficiency in database operations, scoring in the top 10% on Passmark database tests, and high-throughput web serving at 64.48 GB/sec. This resource-dense, general-purpose configuration is highly suited for data-intensive applications, large-scale database hosting, and multi-threaded enterprise workloads that benefit from high-capacity local storage and dedicated CPU resources.
